text:
maya: Quick run this morning comparing flashv2 / flashv3 / triton-vendor across H100 L40 and A100 (q8_static) in us-east, us-west, eu-west. Focused on small (32/64) and medium (128) payloads. p95 + tok/sec below.

diego: Nice. Which batching mode? continuous or per-request? and did you include KV cache warmup?

maya: Continuous batching simulated from trace sampler. included warmup=50 iters. No KV-cache priming beyond that. q8_static symmetric. Quick excerpt of CSV: 

```
# bench cmd
./bench --model redwood-7b --kernels flashv2,flashv3,triton-vendor --gpus H100,A100 --seqs 32,64,128 --regions us-east,eu-west,us-west --q q8 --runs 300 --warmup 50

# results (abridged)
kernel,gpu,region,seq,p95_ms,tokens_sec,err_rate
flashv3,H100,us-east,32,22.4,15000,0.0
flashv2,H100,us-east,32,24.9,13700,0.0
triton-vendor,H100,us-east,32,27.5,12500,0.0
flashv3,A100,us-east,32,28.2,12000,0.0
triton-vendor,A100,us-east,32,26.0,13000,0.0
flashv3,H100,eu-west,64,31.8,9800,0.0
triton-vendor,H100,eu-west,64,90.2,3500,0.07
flashv2,H100,eu-west,64,33.4,9400,0.0
flashv3,H100,us-west,128,48.1,8200,0.0
triton-vendor,H100,us-west,128,41.5,9500,0.0
```

perfbot: uploaded heatmaps and latency timelines for thread 2432109999 -> https://internal.redwood/perf/2432109999 :bar_chart:

nina: Wow eu-west triton-vendor tail on H100 is massive. Looks like driver mismatch + occasional kernel OOM leading to retries. Any logs?

maya: saw a few driver WARNs and a retry loop in the vendor lib logs. attaching short snippet: 

```
[WARN] vendor_kernel: fallback allocation failed, retrying
[ERROR] triton_driver: cuCtxSynchronize timeout
[INFO] request_id=abc123 retry=1
```

diego: Routing thoughts: prefer flashv3 for median payloads (<150 tokens) on H100 everywhere. For A100, triton-vendor can be competitive for small seqs. Heuristic: route to triton-vendor if (gpu == A100 AND seq <= 64 AND vendor_toksec > flashv3_toksec * 1.12). Otherwise prefer flashv3.

maya: Proposal for rollout:
- canary flashv3 3% traffic on H100 us-east/us-west (q8)
- block eu-west triton-vendor until vendor publishes driver patch
- metric checks: kernel_error_rate, p95, 99pct, tokens_sec per kernel, kernel_warmup_time
- hysteresis: expand only after 15min windows x3 show stable improvements, rollback on 3 consecutive 1-min windows with p95 > baseline * 1.15

sre-oncall: Add kernel_tag, kernel_version, driver_version to traces. Also emit kernel_retry_count and kernel_oom_count. We'll wire alerts on kernel_oom_count > 0.

nina: Also run the full quantization QA harness before expanding beyond canary (automated perceptual evals + small human sample set). q8 can shift tokenization edge cases.

maya: Agreed. I'll open a PR to kernel-selector to implement routing heuristic + trace tags. Will include warmup counters and per-kernel cold-start timers.

diego: For eu-west short-term mitigation: prefer flashv2 over triton-vendor for small payloads; flashv3 seems safe but slightly slower there for 64 tokens (but far more stable).

maya: TL;DR: prefer flashv3 on H100 for median/small payloads; use triton-vendor selectively on A100 for very small seq when it measurably outperforms flashv3; hold triton-vendor in eu-west until vendor fixes. Canary + quant QA + tracing + hysteresis. PR by EOD. :white_check_mark:
